exam.title: 2022年6月大学英语四级真题(第1套) 仔细阅读与篇章精研

passages.title: Passage One: Electric Vehicles and the Battery Recycling Challenge
passages.content:
As governments across the globe establish ambitious targets to phase out internal combustion engine vehicles, the electric vehicle (EV) revolution has accelerated dramatically. Automakers are pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into electrification, promising cleaner urban air and substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. Yet, behind this green transportation narrative lies a formidable supply chain hurdle: what should be done with the millions of retired lithium-ion battery packs that will exit service over the next decade?

EV batteries are complex technological marvels, packed with valuable and scarce minerals such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese. Mining these materials exacts heavy environmental and social costs, including groundwater contamination, habitat disruption, and human rights concerns in extractive regions. If discarded batteries are merely deposited in landfills, they pose catastrophic fire hazards and risk leaching toxic heavy metals into adjacent aquifers.

Fortunately, recycling offers a potent solution, effectively closing the loop on critical materials. Advanced hydrometallurgical recycling facilities can now recover up to 95% of battery-grade metals, which can be fed directly back into new cell manufacturing. Such closed-loop systems could slash the demand for virgin mining by more than 30% by 2035.

However, scaling the recycling industry requires overcoming serious economic and logistical hurdles. Standardizing battery pack designs, establishing transparent collection networks, and implementing clear traceability protocols will be imperative to ensure that EV batteries achieve a genuinely sustainable second life.

passages.title: Passage Two: Digital Detox and the Reclamation of Attention
passages.content:
In the contemporary attention economy, our concentration has become the primary commodity mined and monetized by digital tech titans. Notification pings, infinite scroll feeds, and targeted behavioral nudges are engineered by behavioral psychologists to hijack the brain's dopamine reward circuitry. The resulting phenomenon is what cognitive researchers describe as "continuous partial attention"—a fragmented state in which we are perpetually semi-engaged with multiple digital inputs, yet incapable of sustained, deep contemplative thought.

The collateral damage of this attentional fragmentation is profound. Studies demonstrate that it takes an average of twenty-three minutes to regain deep focus after a single digital interruption. Over time, chronic multitasking degrades our working memory capacity and exacerbates subjective feelings of time poverty, leaving people constantly fatigued yet unable to rest.

In reaction to this cognitive overload, a burgeoning movement known as the "digital detox" has emerged. Proponents advocate for establishing sacred, screen-free boundaries: implementing phone-free bedrooms, scheduling weekend digital sabbaticals, and deleting superfluous notification triggers.

While a brief digital hiatus provides welcome immediate relief, long-term cognitive vitality demands structural lifestyle adaptations. Reclaiming one's attention is not about abandoning digital connectivity entirely, but about cultivating intentional agency—ensuring that technology remains an instrument that serves human aspirations rather than an algorithmic master that dictates our consciousness.

questions.stem: What major challenge is accompanying the rapid expansion of electric vehicles?

options.text: A severe shortage of electricity generation worldwide.
Managing and recycling massive numbers of spent batteries.
Public resistance to autonomous driving technology.
The inability of EVs to travel long distances in cold weather.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】事实细节题。第一段末尾提出核心设问'what should be done with the millions of retired lithium-ion battery packs'，指出废旧电池处理是巨大挑战，故选B。

questions.stem: What is the primary objective of tech companies in the attention economy?

options.text: To maximize user attention and monetize it through engagement.
To improve the intellectual sophistication of digital citizens.
To replace all physical schools with virtual education.
To reduce electricity consumption on handheld mobile devices.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】事实细节题。第一段首句即指出'our concentration has become the primary commodity mined and monetized by digital tech titans'，注意力成为被收割与变现的核心商品，故选A。

questions.stem: What risks are associated with landfilled EV batteries according to paragraph 2?

options.text: Immediate explosion of nearby industrial plants.
Fire hazards and toxic heavy metal contamination of groundwater.
Excessive emission of greenhouse gases into the ozone layer.
Accelerated deterioration of nearby power grid cables.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】细节理解题。第二段末句明确提到'pose catastrophic fire hazards and risk leaching toxic heavy metals into adjacent aquifers'（火灾隐患与地下水污染），故选B。

questions.stem: What characterizes 'continuous partial attention' as described in paragraph 1?

options.text: Deep, uninterrupted meditation on philosophical topics.
Being semi-engaged with multiple inputs while unable to focus deeply.
A heightened ability to remember historical facts rapidly.
Complete blindness to environmental physical hazards.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】词义界定题。第一段末尾明确定义为'a fragmented state in which we are perpetually semi-engaged with multiple digital inputs, yet incapable of sustained, deep contemplative thought'，故选B。

questions.stem: What is a major advantage of advanced battery recycling mentioned in paragraph 3?

options.text: It recovers up to 95% of critical metals and reduces virgin mining.
It completely eliminates the cost of manufacturing new EVs.
It doubles the battery capacity of existing vehicles.
It replaces lithium with abundantly available sea water.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】细节事实题。第三段提到'recover up to 95% of battery-grade metals... slash the demand for virgin mining by more than 30%'，故选A。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, how long does it take on average to regain deep focus after an interruption?

options.text: Under two minutes.
About twenty-three minutes.
Over two full hours.
Focus cannot be regained until the next morning.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】事实细节题。第二段清晰指出'it takes an average of twenty-three minutes to regain deep focus after a single digital interruption'，故选B。

questions.stem: What practices are recommended by proponents of the 'digital detox' movement?

options.text: Creating screen-free zones and scheduling periodic digital breaks.
Replacing all smartphones with high-speed laptops.
Answering notifications immediately to reduce backlog.
Checking emails exclusively during the middle of the night.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】细节理解题。第三段列举了'establishing sacred, screen-free boundaries: implementing phone-free bedrooms, scheduling weekend digital sabbaticals'，故选A。

questions.stem: What does the author suggest to facilitate battery recycling in the final paragraph?

options.text: Banning international transport of battery components.
Standardizing pack designs and establishing traceability networks.
Subsidizing fossil fuel extraction to stabilize raw material prices.
Encouraging consumers to dismantle battery packs independently.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】细节推断题。第四段明确提出'Standardizing battery pack designs, establishing transparent collection networks, and implementing clear traceability protocols'，故选B。

questions.stem: What is the author's primary attitude toward the EV revolution?

options.text: Unconditionally celebratory without any criticism.
Completely dismissive and deeply skeptical.
Pragmatic and mindful of supply-chain sustainability.
Indifferent to ecological concerns.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】态度倾向题。作者肯定电动车环保优势的同时，深入剖析电池回收等供应链痛点并提出务实方案，属于理性务实客观（Pragmatic），故选C。

questions.stem: What is the author's ultimate conclusion regarding our relationship with technology?

options.text: Society should completely ban all personal computing devices.
Humans must exercise agency so technology serves us rather than rules us.
Resistance to algorithmic domination is ultimately futile.
Attention fragmentation has no significant impact on health.

questions.explanation: 【考点点拨】主旨升华题。最后一段总结指出'ensuring that technology remains an instrument that serves human aspirations rather than an algorithmic master'，重申发挥自主性让技术服务人类，故选B。
